claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi is a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
The initial alloy has a homogeneous microstructure with minimal pre-existing grain-boundary precipitates or segregation.
Brittle failure in the single-phase high-entropy alloy does not primarily arise from classical grain-boundary segregation or intermetallic precipitation.
Brittle behavior instead arises through threshold-dependent dynamic amorphization of high-angle grain boundaries.
Dynamic grain-boundary amorphization induces localized cavitation.
High strain rates and subambient temperatures favor stress-induced grain-boundary amorphization because conventional ductile mechanisms are suppressed.
Applied stress activates dynamic amorphization at high-angle grain boundaries.
Dynamic amorphization leads to formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline layer.
The ultra-nanocrystalline layer eventually undergoes cavitation and develops nanoporosity.
The amorphization-and-cavitation transition reduces plastic-deformation capacity and promotes brittle failure.
The initial alloy is ductile under moderate strain rates and temperatures.
The alloy undergoes a pronounced loss of toughness after a critical strain or temperature threshold is reached.
After threshold crossing, localized amorphization and nanoporosity will be observed at high-angle grain boundaries.
Conventional alloys tested under the same conditions will not display the localized grain-boundary amorphization and nanoporosity seen in the high-entropy alloy.
The proposed brittle-failure mechanism operates only at high strain or high strain rate and/or low temperature.
Under typical service conditions, the alloy retains a favorable strength–ductility balance.

A controlled comparison with a conventional alloy of analogous grain size can distinguish the proposed mechanism by jointly measuring toughness and grain-boundary evolution under high-rate, low-temperature deformation.

Failure to observe a distinct toughness-loss threshold accompanied by grain-boundary amorphization and cavitation, or observation of the same features in the conventional-alloy control, would falsify the hypothesis.
